children: Oil futures rise after the U.S. struck Iranian rocket launchers which it said were preparing to mine the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran responded firing missiles at U.S. targets in Jordan. The skirmishes "tend to be non-escalatory and the gains tend to be limited," Samer Hasn of XS.com says in a note. Oil prices "may remain stuck in their broad sideways path until elections in Israel and the United States are concluded," he says. Meanwhile there are no signs of a near-term return to negotiations or intentions by either side to make concessions, "keeping escalation risks present." WTI settles up 2.8% at $85.76 a barrel for a 1.3% monthly gain. Front month Brent rises 1.3% to $90.49 for a 0.4% gain in August. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
